All six criteria supported across the answer: overlapping spatial/vector capability, actual guarantees and representative measurement, additional synchronization/operations, index maintenance, duplicate coordination and distribution failure costs. Synchronization plus explained divergent copies supports potential disagreement.

All six criteria supported: replicated copies, communication partition, single-copy consistency versus completion, isolated-reader conflict, configuration-scoped guarantees, requirements/cost/failure reasoning and workload-driven reconsideration without mandatory vendor or multiple stores.

sourceChecks.claim: Live PostgreSQL concepts verifies relational stored data organization. Backup/restore followup verifies regular backups and explicit recovery assumptions; the linked concepts page alone does not establish recovery guarantees.
Live PostgreSQL JSON Types verifies relational JSON support. MongoDB data modeling corroborates query-driven structure and validation; categories therefore do not define exclusive capabilities.

Live MongoDB modeling verifies documents, nested relationships, embedding/reference decisions and access-pattern design; PostgreSQL concepts verifies rows/columns. Direct-key lookup is the defined model, not a claimed product performance guarantee.

Live Cassandra logical modeling explicitly selects one table per query and partition keys from query attributes. Primary Neo4j graph concepts verifies traversal; pgvector README verifies numerical vectors and approximate recall/speed tradeoffs. Cassandra alone is not evidence for the latter two capabilities.

Live PostGIS documentation linked Getting Started verifies enabling its PostgreSQL extension and spatial SQL; pgvector primary README verifies vector columns and nearest-neighbor queries in PostgreSQL.

Live PostgreSQL indexes introduction explains reduced scans and maintenance overhead. MongoDB modeling and the CAP source substantiate duplicate layouts and distributed coordination limits; no cost-free model is asserted.
Live FoundationDB CAP explanation defines completed-write reads, partitioned communication and the conditional consistency/availability conflict, including independent divergent copies.

Live PostgreSQL concepts establishes layout alternatives, not a universal selection recipe. The card is a defensible synthesis of the checked MongoDB query-first modeling, PostgreSQL indexing costs and backup requirements.
